_recorded: 2026-09-08, POST /api/v1/integrations/email/test on a locally built backend (main @ a814a01). Captured from the wire, not written by hand: scripts/refresh-fixtures.mjs issues GET only and refuses non-2xx, and every interesting shape here is a POST error envelope.
_why: The frontend renders whatever this endpoint answers. Four shapes matter, and three of them are failures — the success case is the least informative one, because a probe that works tells the operator nothing they need.

success._note: 204, empty body. The SMTP server accepted the message; delivery is not claimed.

probe_failed._note: 502. `code` is always the literal `probe_failed`; the far end's own text is in `message`. There is NO machine-readable category — an earlier revision emitted one as a prefix and it was withdrawn, because classifying by substring made a host named `smtp.auth-relay.example` report a connection refusal as an auth failure.

body.message: integration probe failed: email send: dial failed: dial tcp: lookup nonexistent.invalid on 127.0.0.11:53: no such host

validation_missing_host._note: 400. Kind validation, not a probe: nothing was dialled.

body.message: validation failed: host: cannot be blank.

validation_tls_none_with_username._note: 400. Plaintext plus a username would offer credentials over an unencrypted connection; CRAM-MD5 hands a hostile server a hash that brute-forces offline. Plaintext WITHOUT a username stays legal — that is an internal relay.

body.message: validation failed: tls_policy: tls_policy must not be "none" when a username is set: credentials would be offered over an unencrypted connection.

validation_bad_recipient._note: 400. `to` is required and validated; the server never infers a recipient from the caller's token.

body.message: validation failed: To: must be a valid email address.
